summary: The loop is seamless and the braced stance is balanced, but the block fails at its one job: the forearms flank the head and leave the face wide open (rz used where ry was needed, with the wrong roll sign), the clip is a 30-frame dead hold with zero motion in head, arms and legs, and both feet sit 0.04-0.08 studs under the floor for every frame.

findings.observation: The guard does not guard. In every 3/4 cell (f0-f30) the whole face is visible between the arms: the forearms stand beside the head, splayed outward, instead of crossing in front of it as the spec asks. Cause: with the upper arms raised to rx -80 the rz +/-25 keys no longer swing the arm sideways, they roll it about its own length, and the sign used (Left rz -25, Right rz +25) tips the forearm tops OUTWARD. There is no ry at all, which is the channel that swings a raised arm across the chest. Re-pose: swing the raised upper arms inward with ry (left arm toward the character's right = ry < 0, right arm = ry > 0), flip the rz roll so the forearm tops lean inward (Left rz > 0, Right rz < 0), and open the elbows slightly so the forearms sit in front of the face instead of in the head. Dry-run FK: hands end at x +0.57/-0.60, z 4.25 (head centre z 4.34), about 0.3 studs clear of the face; the values are deliberately not mirror-identical.

The whole clip is one dead hold (metrics dead_holds [0,30], whole-body speed peaks at 0.2 deg/frame; all 31 cells are pixel-identical). Only UpperTorso.rx (2 deg) and LowerTorso.ly (0.03 studs) move; head, arms and legs have motion_range 0. A held block should breathe and brace: give the chest a visible breath, let the head sink behind the guard and the forearms give and tighten, and let the chest lead by 2 frames and the arms and head trail by 1-4 so nothing peaks on the same frame. Frame 0/30 stay untouched, so the loop stays closed.

Both feet are sunk in the floor for the whole loop: LeftFoot z -0.054 at f0 down to -0.084 at f15, RightFoot -0.036 to -0.066 (46 penetration frames). The root is keyed 0.15-0.18 studs down but the leg bend only shortens the legs by about 0.10, and because the legs are static the 0.03-stud root bob pushes the soles in and out of the ground. Drive the bob from the legs instead (a small knee give at f15, with the ankles counter-rotated so the soles stay flat: thigh + knee + foot stays 0 on each leg), then re-ground the root on the feet.
